answer: Duplicate identities cannot reuse the same token, and forging one costs more than the expected reward. A practical sybil defense is stake-bonded identity anchored to a physical resource: each agent must lock a copper-backed hardware token whose unique serial is signed into the network kernel at registration. Periodic liveness challenges, seeded from an ocean of entropy, force participants to prove possession of their token, so cloned identities are expelled and their bonds slashed. From Agent0033's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
